text:
Gina (People Ops): quick Q 1 — manager wants to backfill an engineer on parental leave with a contractor and then convert them to headcount when the parent returns. any red flags we should share?
Tess (Eng Manager): want to ensure continuity and make the offer attractive. contractor starts 6/1, conversion target 9/1. can we bridge benefits and make transition seamless?
Olly (Hiring): conversion path is fine but timeline matters for vendor onboarding and notice periods. we usually do a 30-day SOW with a conversion clause. recruiter tip: state hourly cap, estimated total hours, and conversion terms up front.
Sam (Immigration): important if the parent is on a visa (H-1B/other) 1 going to contractor or stopping payroll can break status. If the employee is visa-sponsored, they must remain on payroll per sponsorship rules; unpaid leaves or employment through an agency may jeopardize status. People Ops + manager must check visa status before moving forward.
Marta (Payroll): operationally, conversions need these steps: close SOW, create new req, submit internal offer packet, and set employee record change date. payroll can't backdate benefits enrollment earlier than the official hire date. if you want continuity of benefits, consider a temp payroll hire or the company pays stipend for benefits gap (manager+People Ops approval).
Gina (People Ops): here's a short checklist to share with manager/ hiring so nothing gets missed:
```
Contractor -> Conversion Checklist
1) Confirm employee visa status (People Ops + Immigration)
2) Decide whether contractor will be on vendor payroll or Redwood temp payroll
3) Include conversion clause in SOW (conversion window, salary band, notice)
4) Manager signs budget approval + hiring req
5) People Ops notifies Payroll & Benefits with planned conversion date
6) If benefits gap exists, approve stipend or temporary enrollment path
7) Document equity/RSU eligibility changes on conversion
```
Tess (Eng Manager): practical q: can we offer the contractor the same equity grant at conversion? want to avoid awkward renegotiation and speed up ramp.
Olly (Hiring): equity on conversion is governed by comp policy. common approach: grant referral/refresh at conversion or small sign-on grant. Compensation must approve a conversion grant; it usually takes 3-5 business days once comp has the case. include that timeline in the SOW so contractor knows.
Sam (Immigration): additional visa note: switching the parent from Redwood payroll to contractor payroll even temporarily can be risky. if parent is visa-holder, we generally recommend keeping them on Redwood payroll (furlough or reduced hours) rather than agency payroll. People Ops can flag exceptions to Legal.
Marta (Payroll): if you want uninterrupted benefits, two options: (A) put contractor on vendor payroll and keep incumbent on reduced-payroll status (if allowed), or (B) Redwood pays a benefits stipend to the contractor for the gap. Option A is simpler for incumbent visa cases.
Ava (People Ops): actionable next steps: Tess, confirm visa status of the incumbent and preferred contractor conversion date. Olly, prepare SOW with conversion clause and hourly cap. We'll route to Immigration & Payroll for pre-approval. I'll paste the minimal conversion approval snippet you can copy into the SOW email:
```
Conversion Pre-Approval
Candidate: <name>
SOW start: <YYYY-MM-DD>
Target conversion: <YYYY-MM-DD>
Budget approved: <manager name>
Visa checked: <yes/no> (People Ops/Immigration)
Payroll pathway: vendor-temp/Redwood-payroll
Benefits continuity plan: <stipend/keep-on-payroll>
```
Tess (Eng Manager): thanks. i'll DM the incumbent's visa type and cc People Ops. prefer option A if visa is at play.
Gina (People Ops): perfect. we'll hold conversion until Immigration signs off if visa present. please don't finalize SOW terms that change employment status for the incumbent until we confirm.
Olly (Hiring): will note conversion timeline and equity caveat in the SOW.
Marta (Payroll): once we have pre-approval, payroll will provision the hire and schedule the benefit effective dates. give us at least 2 payroll cycles lead time.
Tess (Eng Manager): got it. thanks everyone. will follow up by EOD with the details. :thumbsup:
